claims.text: High-entropy-alloy thermodynamic properties can be determined using a combination of DFT calculations and machine-learning algorithms.
The proposed approach applies across variable high-entropy-alloy compositions and temperatures.
Electronic structure and atomic arrangements are the structural mediators of the proposed approach.
DFT calculations provide accurate electronic structures for high-entropy alloys.
DFT-derived electronic structures can be used to train machine-learning models to predict thermodynamic properties.
The proposed approach will accurately predict melting temperature.
The proposed approach will accurately predict enthalpy and entropy of fusion.
The proposed approach will accurately predict volume change at melting.
The proposed approach will accurately predict liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.
The approach is limited to high-entropy-alloy compositions and temperatures for which DFT calculations are feasible.
Available information is insufficient to determine the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed approach.
Deviation of predicted properties from experimental measurements by more than 10% would rule out the proposed approach.
